question: The First hour of a sitting of the House allotted for asking and answering of questions is called as __________.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Question hour__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The "Question Hour" is a designated period at the beginning of a parliamentary sitting session where members ask questions and the government is obliged to answer them.
 
• This period is crucial for the accountability and transparency of the government, allowing Members of Parliament (MPs) to question the government's decisions and actions.
 
• Question Hour occurs at the start of the day's session, typically lasting for one hour, but the exact timing can vary across different legislative bodies.
 
• It serves as an important tool for legislative oversight, enabling MPs to seek detailed information and clarifications on governmental policies and programs.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Censure motion
 A formal statement of disapproval against a government official or policy, requiring a vote in the legislature.
 
 

 2) Zero hour
 A period following the Question Hour where members can raise matters without any prior notice.
 
 

 3) Privilege motion
 Concerns the breach of parliamentary privileges by a member. It seeks to censure the concerned member if found guilty.
